facts.text: Expert synthesis consistent with Euro NCAP, VaViM and broader work identifies transferable validation methods: scenario-based requirements, parameterized test generation, closed-loop software- and hardware-in-the-loop, deterministic replay, risk-based sampling, regression automation, configuration management, model-credibility arguments, virtual-to-physical correlation and independent spot-checking.

facts.text: The physical content of on-road simulation models does not transfer to off-road machines: machine dynamics, ground interaction, brake response, sensor location and occlusion, target signatures, site geometry and environmental phenomena.

facts.text: NHTSA's heavy-truck experience shows that moving from light road vehicles to heavy road vehicles already required test adaptations for stopping distance and equipment.

facts.text: Moving from roads to deformable quarry surfaces, slopes, berms, piles, articulated frames, implements and airborne contamination is a larger validation change than moving from light road vehicles to heavy road vehicles.

facts.text: Sensor choice changes the virtual-validation credibility plan; because the program's sensors are undecided, the program must be sensor-interface-neutral but not sensor-physics-neutral.

facts.text: The sensor-option guidance specifies what virtual testing and physical correlation must demonstrate, not capabilities that any vendor has already demonstrated.

facts.text: For cameras, virtual testing is particularly good for geometry, object and pose diversity, occlusion, illumination sweeps, algorithm regression and large synthetic scene sets.
facts.quote: | Camera | Geometry, object and pose diversity, occlusion, illumination sweeps, algorithm regression, large synthetic scene sets

facts.text: Camera virtual testing still requires critical physical correlation for photometric realism, glare, darkness, precipitation, dust or mud on the lens, motion blur, machine vibration and actual object appearance.
facts.quote: Photometric realism; glare; darkness; precipitation; dust or mud on the lens; motion blur; machine vibration; actual object appearance

facts.text: For radar and 4D radar, virtual testing is particularly good for range and range-rate geometry, target trajectories, fusion logic and extensive nuisance-object sweeps.
facts.quote: | Radar and 4D radar | Range and range-rate geometry, target trajectories, fusion logic, extensive nuisance-object sweeps

facts.text: Radar and 4D radar virtual testing still requires critical physical correlation for target radar signatures, multipath, material and geometry effects, close-range behavior, installation effects and environmental clutter.
facts.quote: Target radar signatures, multipath, material and geometry effects, close-range behavior, installation effects, environmental clutter

facts.text: For lidar, virtual testing is particularly good for geometry, point-cloud algorithms, occlusion and object-placement combinatorics.
facts.quote: | Lidar | Geometry, point-cloud algorithms, occlusion, object-placement combinatorics

facts.text: Lidar virtual testing still requires critical physical correlation for surface reflectivity, rain, fog and dust attenuation, dirty optical windows, multipath and ghost returns, and real scanner timing.
facts.quote: Surface reflectivity, rain, fog and dust attenuation, dirty optical windows, multipath and ghost returns, real scanner timing

facts.text: For ultrasonic sensors, virtual testing is particularly good for low-speed near-field geometry and control logic.
facts.quote: | Ultrasonic | Low-speed near-field geometry and control logic

facts.text: Ultrasonic virtual testing still requires critical physical correlation for acoustic reflections from irregular materials, ground and implement reflections, temperature, wind and installation effects, and transducer contamination.
facts.quote: Acoustic reflections from irregular materials, ground and implement reflections, temperature, wind and installation effects, transducer contamination

facts.text: For thermal, UWB, GNSS or tag-based, infrastructure-assisted sensor options, virtual testing is particularly good for sensor fusion and deterministic location and identity scenarios.

facts.text: Thermal, UWB, GNSS or tag-based, infrastructure-assisted sensor options still require critical physical correlation for site infrastructure failure modes, tag coverage, non-equipped objects, and installation and maintenance assumptions.
